name: Neive
shape: Eurostat LAU, the commune it is named for

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
Denominazione di Origine Controllata. The label names a precise area, and the wine is tested during production.
Indicazione Geografica Tipica, Italy's broad regional tier.
An aged Italian wine. Chianti Riserva needs at least 6 months in barrel and 3 more in bottle before release.

notes: Barbaresco, from Nebbiolo, is fairly light in color and body but very well structured and aromatic.
It smells of roses or violets, with cherry, truffle, fennel and licorice, and turns smoky, earthy and leathery with age.
It is very tannic and tight when young and is usually best 5 to 10 years after the vintage.
Its tannins soften sooner than Barolo's, so it is more approachable young but usually ages less long.
Neive makes the most full bodied and tannic Barbaresco, and Treiso the lightest and finest.

blurb.text: A Barbaresco commune in Piedmont. Barbaresco is a Nebbiolo wine from the Langhe, east of Alba, and its zone takes in all of Neive, Barbaresco and Treiso and part of Alba. The wine is often compared with Barolo.
